key_insight: The paper introduces a unified analytical framework that diagnoses where photoelectrochemical cell efficiency is lost and turns that diagnosis into rational design guidance for both BIJ and SEJ devices.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical way to fit experimental I–V curves, quantify loss channels, and compare materials and architectures to guide targeted improvements in PEC systems.
method: Build a physically consistent loss model for BIJ and SEJ photoelectrodes.
Generate I–V curves, efficiency maps, and Sankey energy-flow diagrams under ideal and real conditions.
Fit experimental data to decompose losses into thermodynamic, optical, recombination, and interfacial terms.
evidence_signal: The framework is validated against literature results across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries, and used to compare absorber classes such as Si, perovskites, hematite, and BiVO4.
watch_item: The model’s usefulness depends on the quality of experimental I–V data and on whether its simplifying assumptions capture complex real-device interfaces and transport effects.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
